name: Peruvannamuzhi Dam & Spice Park
tagline: Reservoir, spice gardens and solar-boat tours in Kozhikode’s ecotourism hub
summary: Peruvannamuzhi Dam & Spice Park is a hill‑fringed reservoir with boating, spice‑garden attractions and wildlife facilities — best enjoyed in the cool, dry season.
description: Peruvannamuzhi sits in the eastern hills of Kozhikode district and centres on the Kuttiyadi/Peruvannamuzhi reservoir. The site combines a scenic dam and lake, small forest islands, a crocodile shelter and birdwatching areas with nearby spice research farms and demonstration gardens.

Kerala Tourism develops Peruvannamuzhi as an ecotourism hub: the tourism department has added picnic amenities, an interpretation area and solar‑boat initiatives to reduce the site’s footprint. The reservoir is also inside/adjacent to the Malabar Wildlife Sanctuary, giving visitors good chances for nature and birding walks.

Visitors come for short boat trips to islands, quiet launches across the lake, gentle treks at the forest edge and spice‑garden viewpoints that show pepper, cardamom, cinnamon and other crops. The spot works well as a half‑day or full‑day outing from Kozhikode.
highlights: Scenic reservoir with island dotted lake and dam views
Boat trips (speedboat, rowboat, and expanding solar‑boat services)
Spice garden area and nearby ICAR/IISR experimental farm
Birdwatching, crocodile shelter and small wildlife displays
Picnic lawns, interpretation centre and children's park

sections.heading: Background
body: Peruvannamuzhi (Peruvannamoozhy) grew as an ecotourism site around the Kuttiyadi irrigation reservoir. The Kerala Tourism department lists the dam and reservoir as a key nature destination in Kozhikode and has invested in visitor facilities and sustainable boating to encourage low‑impact tourism.

The area also hosts agricultural and spice‑research activity — local demonstration gardens and experimental plots linked to the Indian Institute of Spices Research and Krishi Vigyan Kendra support both research and visitor education.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Take a boat across the reservoir to view the island memorial garden and to reach small forest islets; boat services include rowboats, launches and an expanding fleet of solar boats (operations depend on season and water levels).

Visit the spice‑garden areas and nearby research farms to learn about pepper, cardamom, cinnamon and other spices grown in the Western Ghats; pair a garden stroll with birdwatching or a short walk to the crocodile shelter and wildlife displays.

Combine a calm lake cruise with a drive up to nearby Kakkayam or a short forest trek into the Malabar Wildlife Sanctuary for broader wildlife and hill views. The interpretation centre and landscaped picnic spaces make the site family‑friendly.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best time: the cool, dry season (post‑monsoon months) when trails are dry and boating is usually available — boating may be suspended during and immediately after heavy monsoon rains, so confirm services before you travel.

Getting there: Peruvannamuzhi lies roughly 55–60 km by road from Kozhikode city (about 1.5–2 hours depending on traffic). Local buses and private vehicles connect via Perambra/Kuttiady; the nearest major rail and air links are at Kozhikode. On‑site facilities have been renovated and expanded under Kerala Tourism but opening and service details (boat schedules, island access, guided garden visits) vary by season — confirm locally.

latest.text: Kozhikode district administration announces restart and expansion of boating at Peruvannamuzhi reservoir, mandating eco‑friendly solar boats and approving a new boating point at Thonikadavu (Heart Island).

Kerala Tourism inaugurates renovated visitor facilities at Peruvannamuzhi (children’s park, interpretation centre, cafeteria, landscaped walkways) and flags off solar‑boat services as part of an eco‑friendly upgrade.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Cool, dry season after the southwest monsoon (roughly September–March); confirm boating before you go.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Drive or take a bus from Kozhikode (about 55–60 km / 1.5–2 hours). Local buses and hired taxis connect via Perambra/Kuttiady; nearest rail/airport at Kozhikode — confirm connections locally.
etiquette: Confirm boating operations and island access ahead — services vary with reservoir levels and season.
Wear sturdy shoes and carry rain protection in shoulder seasons; the sun can be strong on the water—bring sun protection.
Do not feed or disturb wildlife; follow sanctuary rules and keep the site litter‑free.
Buy spices from authorised stalls or the research farm outlet if you want fresh, labelled samples; check packaging for origin.
